summary: The exact Git identity, archive checksum, staged receipt, focused tests, dependency order, and live accepted-shot evidence verify. Approval is nevertheless fail-closed because the delivered player violates the plan's Unity 2019.3.4f1 pin, the archive embeds an untracked wrapper that is absent from the reviewed HEAD, and the collector mutates accepted-shot metadata after the atomic publication rename required by Todo 5.

blocking_findings.criterion: exact plan compliance and Unity compatibility
blocking_findings.description: The governing plan requires the staged player build entry point to be pinned to Unity 2019.3.4f1. The reviewed project, build script, publication receipt, reproducibility receipt, and archive identity instead use Unity 2019.4.41f2 changeset 6b23d448b533, with no plan amendment authorizing that migration.
blocking_findings.required_resolution: Rebuild and prove the staged player with the plan-pinned 2019.3.4f1 editor, or formally amend and re-review the plan before accepting a 2019.4.41f2 artifact.

blocking_findings.description: scripts/build_physics_player.sh copies scripts/9001-player-wrapper.sh into the payload as 9001.x86_64, but that source file is untracked and absent from HEAD. The on-disk wrapper and embedded archive member both hash to cff7f36268fd29831e0ab0ac6c952379b390c87bb7b1f152962b87322ec801d1. The archive therefore cannot be reconstructed from the reviewed Git object alone even though the retained two-build receipt reports matching outputs.
blocking_findings.required_resolution: Commit every build input, rebuild from a clean checkout of the reviewed commit, and regenerate provenance and two-build reproducibility receipts.

blocking_findings.description: Todo 5 requires the complete shot to be validated in shot_NNN.tmp and then atomically renamed to shot_NNN. The collector validates and writes metadata in the temporary directory, renames it, then rewrites path-bearing metadata, revalidates, and writes metadata.json again at the published path. Consumers can therefore observe a renamed accepted directory while its final metadata is still being changed.
blocking_findings.required_resolution: Produce final path-stable metadata and complete final validation before the single rename, with a regression test proving no accepted-shot file is opened for writing after publication.

todo_results.note: Frozen capture contract and fixtures verify.
Exporter evidence passes under the migrated Unity project, but the migration is not an amendment to the Todo 7 editor pin.
Contacts, support, and macro-event tests and evidence pass.
Versioned bridge and synchronized capture tests pass.
Accepted metadata is mutated after the publication rename.
Opt-in launcher guardrails and command generation pass.
The artifact uses the wrong Unity pin and depends on an untracked build input.
A live accepted shot verifies same-frame RGB/state, ordered clocks/events, entities, energy, and staged provenance.
Current task-8-smoke.json carries the staged digest and all 10 documentation verifier tests pass.
Opt-in immutable supervision loading and legacy defaults pass focused tests.

dependency_and_commit_order.note: Todo 10 precedes dependent Todo 9, and all reviewed todo commits are ancestry ordered.

verification.detail: HEAD and tree match the reviewed identity.
Expected SHA succeeds; deliberately wrong SHA fails closed.
Contract, bridge, collector, validator, launcher, package, smoke, deterministic-build, loader, and documentation groups pass in the final replay.
Reviewed build, collection, and wrapper scripts pass bash -n.
One state and seven events validate with exact RGB/state render_frame 16642 and archive provenance.
The embedded executable wrapper source is absent from HEAD.
Published metadata is rewritten after rename.

additional_findings: Archive verification and extraction do not fully constrain member types, expansion size, duplicate names, or provenance-derived paths.
Some receipts authenticate claims using other files from the same evidence set rather than an independent trust anchor.
F2 reports additional runtime, timeout, JSON escaping, path-confinement, and failure-atomic packaging defects; those reinforce rejection but are not required to establish this F1 verdict.
